item.text: {"representations":[{"case_ref":"sample_3159a77476d400f2","text":"Across March 30–April 12, steps abruptly fell from the 28-day baseline mean of 7,998 to 2,321/day (−71%), and active minutes from 55.2 to 4.9/day (−91%). Both stayed low throughout all 14 days, including weekends, without recovery; recorded activity at 21:00 shortened from 50–60 to 0–10 minutes. Low movement remained similar: 447.5 versus 450.5 minutes/day, in ten daytime bouts separated by five-minute gaps, rather than one continuous interval. Sleep also remained stable at 469.4 versus 470.5 minutes, with starts at 22:42–22:58 and waking consistently at 07:00; weekday/weekend differences were small. Resting heart rate averaged 56.3 versus 56.1 bpm and RMSSD 44.8 versus 45.3 ms, staying within baseline ranges. Their daily association became moderately inverse (r=−0.59); activity versus next-wake-date sleep was weak (r=0.32, 13 pairs), and steps versus active minutes was negligible. No metrics were missing, with consistent wear coverage."},{"case_ref":"sample_7de66e1de896dc00","text":"During March 30–April 12, sleep and steps shifted abruptly and remained below the preceding 28-day baseline on every day, including weekends, without recovery. Sleep averaged 330.9 versus 468.5 minutes (−137.7 minutes, −29%), ranging 322–338 minutes. Sleep starts moved from about 22:51 to 01:09, approximately 138 minutes later, while waking stayed at 07:00. Steps averaged 2,643 versus 7,985/day (−67%), with little subsequent trend. Despite fewer steps, active minutes remained 55.4 versus 54.4/day, with continuous 50–60-minute intervals starting at 21:00. Low movement stayed near baseline (451.1 versus 448.6 minutes), distributed across ten daytime bouts with five-minute gaps. Resting heart rate rose gradually from 55 to mostly 57 bpm, averaging 56.3 versus 55.9; all four weekend values were 57. RMSSD remained 44.9 ms in both periods. Activity versus next-wake-date sleep was weak (r=−0.15, 13 pairs), and heart rate versus RMSSD was negligible. All metrics were observed with adequate coverage."},{"case_ref":"sample_ac1d07ee01bc3c76","text":"March 30–April 12 introduced a repeating weekday/weekend sleep split absent from the 28-day baseline. Baseline sleep averaged 468.8 minutes, starting near 22:51 and ending at 07:00 in both groups. All ten window weekdays had 386–393 minutes (mean 389.9, −78.8), starting at 00:07–00:14 and ending at 07:00. Both weekends had 565–575 minutes (mean 569.8, +100.9), starting at 01:05–01:15 and ending at 11:00; shorter weekday sleep resumed April 6. The overall mean of 441.3 minutes and positive slope therefore obscure this recurring pattern rather than indicate sustained recovery. Other means stayed close to baseline: steps 7,939 versus 8,019/day, active minutes 54.7 versus 55.4, low movement 451.4 versus 451.0, heart rate 56.1 versus 56.5 bpm, and RMSSD 45.4 versus 45.3 ms. Activity remained at 21:00; interrupted low-movement bouts began at 11:30 on weekends versus 10:00 weekdays. Activity versus next-wake-date sleep was weak (r=−0.15).
